targetTexts.2: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
targetTexts.3: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.
targetTexts.4: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,
targetTexts.5: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
targetTexts.6: Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,
targetTexts.7: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’
targetTexts.8: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
targetTexts.9: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
targetTexts.10: His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
targetTexts.11: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
targetTexts.12: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,
targetTexts.13: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,
targetTexts.14: yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.
targetTexts.15: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.
targetTexts.16: He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.
targetTexts.17: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
targetTexts.18: He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.
targetTexts.19: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
targetTexts.20: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
targetTexts.21: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
targetTexts.22: In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.
targetTexts.23: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.
targetTexts.24: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
targetTexts.25: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.
targetTexts.26: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
targetTexts.27: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
targetTexts.28: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
targetTexts.29: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
